title: The one who does not arrive
theme: One without understanding, without a held mind, always impure, does not reach that place, but comes back into saṃsāra.

words.context: Śaṅkara: the rider with such a charioteer («न सः रथी»)

sandhi.rule: Visarga before t becomes s, P. 8.3.34 (विसर्जनीयस्य सः); u and i before a dissimilar vowel become v and y, P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि); n of -vān stays before bh.

sandhi.type: saḥ before a consonant; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: saḥ loses its ending before a consonant, P. 6.1.132 (एतत्तदोः सुलोपोऽकोरनञ्समासे हलि). Final m stays before a vowel.
Final m → anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः); a + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).

samasa.meaning: one who has no (held) mind; with the suffix -ka

morphology.note: A bahuvrīhi of a- and manas with the suffix -ka; the commentators take it not as ‘mindless’ but as one whose mind is not held.
Present of gam with adhi, ‘go towards, attain’; the same verb that names attaining the goal is here used of falling back into saṃsāra.

translation.literal: ‘But he who is without understanding, without [a held] mind, always impure, does not reach that place, and enters saṃsāra.’
translation.readable: ‘One who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held and who is never pure, does not reach that goal, but comes back again into the round of births.’

anvaya: यः तु अविज्ञानवान् अमनस्कः सदा अशुचिः भवति, सः तत् पदम् न आप्नोति, संसारम् च अधिगच्छति ॥
syntax: A relative clause (yas tu … bhavati) with three predicates (avijñānavān, amanaskaḥ, aśuciḥ); the main clause has two verbs, the negated āpnoti and adhigacchati, joined by ca.

ambiguities.note: The letters सदाशुचिः can be read sadā śuciḥ or sadā aśuciḥ; the sense here, and the contrast with 1.3.8, require sadā aśuciḥ. The vishvAsa mūla and Raṅgarāmānuja’s text mark the elided a with avagraha (सदाऽशुचिः).

Śaṅkara: in 1.3.5–6 the charioteer; here the rider who has such a charioteer, «न सः रथी तत् पूर्वोक्तमक्षरं यत्परं पदम् आप्नोति तेन सारथिना». Raṅgarāmānuja: these two verses give the outcome of controlling the senses or not, «वशीकरणतदभावयोः प्रयोजनं दर्शयति मन्त्रद्वयेन».

beginner: The chariot was going somewhere. This verse says what happens when the journey fails. A person who lacks understanding, who never steadies the mind and whose life is not clean does not arrive at the goal. Worse, says the verse, such a person goes round again into saṃsāra, the cycle of birth and death. Śaṅkara explains that 'that goal' is the imperishable, highest place spoken of earlier, and saṃsāra is marked by birth and death. Raṅgarāmānuja adds that such a person does not merely fail to arrive: the uncontrolled horses actually drag them into the thick forest of saṃsāra. The word 'impure' is explained by him as a mind always leaning towards wrong thoughts. The verse is less a threat than a statement of where an unguided journey ends: back where it started.
analogy: Like a carriage whose horses have the bit between their teeth: not only does it miss the town it set out for, it ends up lost in the woods.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: That one without understanding, without a held mind and always impure does not reach that place, and enters saṃsāra.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: This is the result for the rider whose charioteer lacks understanding, «पूर्वोक्तस्याविज्ञानवतो बुद्धिसारथेरिदं फलमाह»: ‘that place’ is the imperishable, highest place spoken of before, «तत् पूर्वोक्तमक्षरं यत्परं पदम्»; not only does he not reach it, he enters saṃsāra, marked by birth and death.

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Commenting on 1.3.7–8 together: ‘impure’ because always inclined to contrary thoughts, «सर्वदा विपरीतचिन्ताप्रवणत्वात्»; not merely failing to reach the goal, the senses lead into the dense wilderness of saṃsāra, «प्रत्युत गहनं संसारकान्तारमेव प्रापयति».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: In our source Madhva prints 1.3.3–1.3.11 without comment and then comments once, marking it ॥ १०-१२ ॥, on the deities who preside over the senses, their objects, the mind and the intellect; he does not gloss this verse. His digital text keys यस्तवविज्ञानवान् for yas tv avijñānavān, a witness error (corrections.json).

advaita.text: The rider with an undiscerning charioteer does not reach the imperishable highest place, and enters saṃsāra, «जन्ममरणलक्षणम्».

visistadvaita.text: Uncontrolled senses not only fail to reach the goal but lead into the wilderness of saṃsāra, «गहनं संसारकान्तारमेव प्रापयति».

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara and Raṅgarāmānuja agree on the sense; they differ on what ‘that place’ finally is (the imperishable Brahman; Viṣṇu’s highest place, as Raṅgarāmānuja says on 1.3.3). In our source Madhva prints 1.3.3–1.3.11 without comment and then comments once, marking it ॥ १०-१२ ॥, on the deities who preside over the senses, their objects, the mind and the intellect; he does not gloss this verse.

contemporary.text: ‘Comes back into the round’ describes something familiar on a small scale too: a direction never held tends to return to where it began. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: What journeys of yours have ended back at the start, and why?
reflect.deeper: Why does the verse add ‘impure’ to ‘without understanding’ and ‘without a held mind’?
reflect.practice: Name one aim you keep returning to without reaching, and one thing that pulls you off it.

flags.note: Madhva’s digital text keys यस्तवविज्ञानवान् (witness error, corrections.json).
madhva.json files Madhva’s single comment on 1.3.10–11 (his mark ॥ १०-१२ ॥) under every mantra from 1.3.3 to 1.3.11; it is not quoted here.
